internal_alignment: RL.1.1: ask and answer questions about key details in a story (Page 1). RL.1.2: retell a story (Page 5: Beginning, Middle, End, independent). RL.1.3: say who is in the story, where it happens, what happens, and why a character acts (Pages 2, 3, and 4: character motivation, cause and effect, sequencing a problem and its resolution). RL.1.7: use pictures plus story details to describe the story (throughout; every story has a scene picture, and Page 4 is four illustrated panels). The stories use familiar Grade 1 vocabulary and high-frequency words rather than staying tightly inside the phonics scope, at the user's direction, so they read as real stories. Every inference is grounded in the text; no prediction. Internal record only; no standards codes appear on any child page, and no separate answer key is published for this pack.
pack: Grade 1 Reading: Read and Think: Understanding Stories

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story, then writes a word from the word bank. Supported. The "first" question forces tracking the order of events, not just spotting an object.
answers: What day does Nina go to the park? Saturday
What does Nina put in the wagon first? Her toys
Who does Nina see at the park? Leo
What do Nina and Leo play with? The blue ball
pages_detail.title: Key Details

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story, then explains why Milo acts, with sentence starters. Guided.
answers: Milo takes the puppy home because it is all alone (accept: it has no home, it is lost)
Milo is glad because the puppy found its home
pages_detail.title: Why Does Milo Help?

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story, draws a line to match each cause to its effect, then writes one why. Guided. The chain is connected: sun, dry soil, water, tall plants, picked flowers.
answers: The sun is hot. goes to The soil gets dry.
Ruby gives the plants water. goes to The plants grow tall and strong.
The plants grow tall. goes to Ruby picks red flowers.
Ruby gives the plants water because the soil is dry
pages_detail.title: What Makes It Happen?

pages_detail.activities: Four story panels in mixed order. The child reads each part and writes 1, 2, 3, or 4 in its circle. The two "puts a block on top" panels look alike, so the child must read the size words and the outcomes to order them.
answers: Oscar builds a tall tower. is 1 (beginning)
He puts a big block on top. is 2
Oscar builds the tower again with a small block on top. The tower stands tall. is 4 (resolution)
pages_detail.title: Put the Story in Order

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the story, answers one text-grounded inference with no starter, then retells it in writing: Beginning, Middle, End. The boxes are open with a small word bank only. Independent.
answers: Why does Ivy run to get her dad? She cannot reach the balloon (accept: it is too high for her)
Beginning: Ivy takes her balloon to the park
Middle: the wind blows it into a tree, she cannot reach it, she runs for Dad
End: Dad reaches up, gets the balloon, gives it back, Ivy holds it tight
pages_detail.title: Retell and Think
